property.disabled.name: Disabled
property.speed.name: Speed
property.speed.desc: Here you can choose a speed limit for an adjacent path. "0" is unlimited.
property.prop.OUTPUT.name: Redstone Output
property.prop.OUTPUT.desc: Here you can set the redstone output. For example, for switch control
property.prop.INPUT.blocking.name: Blocking
property.prop.INPUT.blocking.desc: Blocks a path. Paths can be blocked directly behind a signal or on an empty field (e.g. for permanent blockage)
property.prop.INPUT.resetting.name: Resetting
property.prop.INPUT.resetting.desc: Resets a path. Paths are reset directly in front of a signal or on an empty piece (e.g. for partial path resolution)
property.pathway_costs.name: Additional pathway costs
property.pathway_costs.desc: This option can be used to increase the 'costs' for certain path elements so that the path algorithm avoids this path if possible. This is particularly helpful if you want to influence the pathway manually.
property.ZS32.name: Zs Signals
property.ZS32.desc: §nZs2 Direction indicator§r: The Zs2 indicates the direction of the track through a code letter.%n§nZs3 Speed indicator§r: The Zs3 indicates the speed that must not be exceeded from the signal on the subsequent switch area or until the next main signal through a code number.%n§nZs6 Change of track indicator§r: The track leads to the opposite track.%n§nZs8 Opposite track replacement signal§r: The track leads from the disturbed signal to the opposite track.%n§nZs13 Dead-end track and early stop indicator§r: Travel to a track with shortened entrance track or to a dead-end track.%n§nZp8 Close doors§r: The signal is given by the train conductor and the driver of the multiple unit is to close the doors.%n§nZp9 Departure§r: The signal is given by the train conductor and the driver of the multiple unit is to depart.
property.delay.name: Delay time
property.delay.desc: Here you can set a time from 0 to 60 seconds in which the route definition is to be delayed. This is particularly useful for railroad crossings.
property.prop.SIGNAL.name: Signal
property.prop.SIGNAL.desc: Here you choose the associated signal in the world.
property.presignals.name: Define Presignals
property.presignals.desc: Here you can define corresponding distant signals that also activate when the main signal is in the driving position, even without an active pathway.
property.can_be_overstepped.name: Can be skipped
property.can_be_overstepped.desc: The signal can be skipped. This means that the pathway can be set to the next signal and this signal shows identifier light (turned off).
property.protectionway.name: Overlap
property.protectionway.desc: Select a section of path behind the destination signal. The overlap is set up to this point. The overlap (pass-through path) is a protective section behind the destination signal that must be secured and kept clear if trains do not come to a stop in front of the signal as planned and path-through past the signal.
property.reset_protectionway_delay.name: Delay-Overlap-reset
property.reset_protectionway_delay.desc: Sets a delay during which the overlap is to be reset after the specified sensor has been passed.
Select a redstone input which will trigger the overlap reset.
property.zs6_state.name: Wrong side of tracks (Zs6)
property.zs6_state.desc: Here you can select whether the path leads to the wrong side of tracks.
property.signal_repeater.name: Signal repeater
property.signal_repeater.desc: Here you can define whether the distant signal is a repeater or not. If the distant signal is a repeater, the corresponding indicator light also comes on.
property.inconnection.name: Incoming connection
property.inconnection.desc: Specify the signal to which the incoming driving path is to be set here. You can get the coordinates by right-clicking on the respective signal in the signal box.
property.prop.SIGNALBOX.name: Signalbox
property.prop.SIGNALBOX.desc: Select the signal box here. You must then close and reopen the window to select the appropriate input connection.
gui.signalbridge.edit.desc: In edit mode, the signal bridge can be assembled from individual blocks. To do this, various blocks can be selected on the right edge and placed in the grid. Then use CTRL and right-click to select a 'start block', i.e. the block that will be placed in the position you looking at.
